 Indian skipper Lakshya Raichandani lifts the coveted trophy before sharing it with his teammates. The champions then gather for photographs in front of the winners' backdrop, as fireworks and confetti add to the spectacle, making it a memorable celebration for the Indian camp. The young Indian champions erupt into chants of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" , celebrating their memorable triumph with immense pride and passion. Beating Pakistan in a tournament final makes this triumph even more special for the young Indian players. They will be well aware of the significance of this achievement, and their phones are likely to be flooded with congratulatory messages and calls as they soak in a memorable victory at such a young age. It was an absolute pleasure bringing you all the action from this thrilling contest. We hope you enjoyed every bit of the coverage as much as we enjoyed bringing it to you. This is Nikhil Jadhav signing off, along with Ramakrishnan MS, Abhinand Raghavendran and Praveen Kumar. That's all from us. Until next time, goodbye, take care and stay safe, everyone! Lakshya Raichandani | India captain: [Take me through your emotions in those last few overs] Yeah, but we were quite optimistic and we didn't stop believing and yeah, it was a roller-coaster match. [You think it's too much that you gave away?] No, no, we always had the belief that we will chase down because the wicket was good. And yeah, we had always belief. [Were you surprised with the lower-order batsmen?] No, I always believed in them. We are playing with eight, nine, almost eleven batters, so I wasn't surprised. [Any message you want to give to all the Indian fans?] Yeah, just thank you for the support and keep supporting us. It's now India's turn to collect their winners' medals, with skipper Lakshya Raichandani leading the way. Vice-captain Yashbardhan Chauhan follows, while Player of the Tournament Aaryavir Sehwag is next to receive his medal. Anvay Dravid, Mohit Ulva and the rest of the Indian squad are also making their way forward to collect their honours. The Indian team's support staff are also honoured with their medals, completing the medal ceremony for the champions. Farhan Yousaf | Pakistan captain: I think that was a good enough total but India played excellent cricket. [Where did things go wrong today?] All the boys were doing perfect but unfortunately we were wayward with our bowling. That's why we lost the match. [On the slow over-rate] Yes, obviously we go with the three pacers and obviously all the pacers taking time. That's why we were too late. And at the end we just plan according to the situation. That's why we were getting late. [Do you have a message for the Pakistan fans?] Thank you for the support and keep supporting Pakistan. The Pakistani players are now making their way forward to receive their runners-up medals. Pakistan captain Yousaf leads the way, becoming the first to collect his medal, with his teammates following suit. The team's support staff will receive their medals next. Aaryavir Sehwag | Player of the Tournament: [Discussion in the dressing room before the run-chase] The discussion was the wicket is very good to bat on and it's not a huge score and if we just normally bat and play our conventional shots, we'll get to the score. And there was always a belief that we'll chase it down. [You didn't think about changing the game-plan given that the target was quite high?] No, not really because we know, we talk in our team meetings and we talk about how we can chase 100 or 120 runs in the last 10 overs because the wicket was very good to bat on as well. So someone had to bat deep. And Lakshya did that. So hats off to him. And obviously, what Mohit and Manal did at the end was absolutely amazing and hats off to them as well. [Have you spoken to your dad yet?] No, sir, I haven't. I will later. Mohit Ulva | Player of the Final: [Working on his batting in the nets] Yeah, obviously (laughs). [On his emotions while going into bat today] My team and my head coach had belief in me. Also I had belief in me. So that's it. [Last over, what were you telling yourself?] Nothing, I just saw the ball and hit the ball. Time for the presentations now... Aaryavir Sehwag (translated from Hindi): I'm not feeling any pain now. There's no pain anymore. I'm feeling really happy. We've forgotten all about the pain and everything else. This is an absolutely incredible victory. We had been sitting inside for a long time, praying to God. Honestly, it felt like a miracle. I still have goosebumps. I can't believe what I witnessed as a spectator because I was watching everything from the outside. It's an unbelievable feeling. I really enjoyed it. [Batting through pain in the final. What kept you going?] The emotions are obviously very intense, especially when it's an India-Pakistan match, and I'm playing for India. This was my second India-Pakistan match. Unfortunately, I got out early in the first one, so naturally, I wanted to do something special for my team this time. I was in a lot of pain, but I didn't want to walk off the field. I knew that if I continued batting, I would somehow keep putting pressure on the Pakistani bowling attack, and I wanted to dominate them. Whatever contribution I was able to make towards this victory, I'm extremely grateful for it. [What does this final victory mean to you?] I'm honestly short of words. I really don't know what to say because this feeling is incredible. Hats off to Ulwa and Manal for the way they played. It was absolutely unbelievable. I'm genuinely speechless. I can't even describe it. All I can say is that I thoroughly enjoyed this moment! Arjun Rajput (translated from Hindi): We have successfully achieved the target we came here with. The way the team chased such a big total and finished the game was outstanding. Hats off to Manal, Ulva, Sehwag, Lakshya, the captain, and everyone in the support staff. Everyone did a great job. [India vs Pakistan final - handling the nerves and pressure of chasing a big total] There was little pressure because it was a final, and we were chasing a huge target of 330 runs. But everyone believed that we could chase it down. The team got off to a very good start, and then everyone kept contributing along the way. The partnership and the chase by Manal and Ulva towards the end were excellent. [Dressing-room atmosphere after two consecutive wickets fell at 217] Nothing much. We simply had the belief that whoever went in next would finish the game. We had tremendous trust in one another and every player went out there with that same belief and confidence. That's what helped us get through. It was really wonderful. Ulva (2/2): [Batting at number 10] Number 10 has actually always been a lucky number for me because most of my runs have come when I've batted at number 10. So, I guess that's how it is. [Discussions during the innings break] It was very simple. They had scored the runs, and we believed we could score them too. We had confidence in our batting because we have a strong batting line-up. Looking at the pitch, we knew it was completely flat. We felt that if we had wickets in hand, we could get the job done. Lakshya set up the innings beautifully and played really well. Unfortunately, he got out; otherwise, he would have finished the game himself. But everyone believed in themselves. We all knew we could do it, and the coach had confidence in us too. Before I went out to bat, sir personally came up to me and said, "You can do it. Just believe in yourself." So, I went out there and simply watched the ball and hit the ball. I wasn't thinking about what was happening or what might happen next. I wasn't overthinking anything. I was just watching the ball and playing my shots. Mohit Ulva (translated from Hindi) (1/2): [What was going through your mind during that final over?] Nothing much. I just had belief in myself and faith in God. My Asia Cup hadn't been particularly great until then. I knew I was a bowler, but I also believed that I was an all-rounder. However, I hadn't got enough opportunities to prove myself yet. But I always believed that I could do it. I just needed Manal's support. The momentum he created by going out to bat before me and setting things up was incredible. I just had to go out there and deliver. [On hitting the winning runs] Nothing much. I was just waiting for that one ball. I knew I could hit a boundary and finish the game. I had complete faith in God. I knew it was my day and I would finish the game. I have always believed in myself. I keep telling myself, "I can do it, I will do it, and I will get it done right till the end." And coming to Venkata, he gave me a lot of confidence, especially. He kept telling me, "No, you can do it. Just go out and play. You will finish it." The belief he gave me, that the two of us could get the job done on the last ball, strengthened my own confidence. I believed that if I stayed there until the final ball, I would finish the game. Manal Chauhan (translated from Hindi): I was very focused. At that time, Ulva came to bat, he only said that we can finish. Just trust your process, trust yourself. [The finisher's role - recalling an earlier interview during the tournament and the support staff's faith in his role] Yes, for that, I would really like to thank the support staff as well. They believed in me as a finisher, and the coach showed a lot of trust in me. They backed me right till the end. They told me just one thing - once you go out to the middle, simply enjoy yourself and play your game [Chasing more than 100 runs with limited time at the crease – calculations, run rate and batting approach] At that moment, I just had faith in myself. I was doing the calculations as I went along. I felt that even if I managed to hit just one boundary in an over and take four singles, we could comfortably maintain a run rate of 10 runs per over. So, the only thing on my mind was to make sure I hit at least one good shot every over. [Getting dismissed against spin] Yes, at that moment, I was putting a little too much pressure on myself. When I went inside, I even had a few tears in my eyes because opportunities like these don't come very often, and we had come so close to winning the match. Let's not overlook the efforts of Indian openers Raichandani and Sehwag, who laid a solid foundation at the top of the order. The duo displayed tremendous maturity and composure, providing India with the perfect platform to build their chase in such a high-pressure final. Credit must also go to Kavya Patel and Venkata, who made significant contributions with the ball earlier in the day, claiming four and three wickets respectively to restrict the opposition in the closing stages. Pakistan looked set to breach the 350-run mark after the start they got off to, but India's bowlers did well to rein them in during the closing stages, preventing them from posting an even more imposing total. Let's now turn our attention to the young Indian stars as they share their thoughts. The players look thrilled, enjoying the moment as they interact with the presenter. 17:14 Local Time, 13:14 GMT, 18:44 IST: Give me a moment to take it all in, because this is truly a special moment. Ulva is racing around the field with the Indian flag draped around him. It's an incredible sight and one that will take a while to sink in! A number 10 batter hammering 49 runs off just 26 deliveries in an India-Pakistan final. You don't get to witness something like this every day. India looked to be virtually out of the contest when Anvay Dravid was run out in the 37th over. However, what unfolded thereafter was nothing short of extraordinary, with hardly anyone anticipating such a dramatic turnaround. It was the crucial stand between Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva that completely changed the complexion of the game. Their 57-run partnership breathed life into India's chase, keeping them in the contest and taking the match down to the wire. Even after losing his partner Manal Chauhan in the 48th over, Mohit Ulva refused to throw in the towel. Venkata also chipped in with some valuable runs, but it was Ulva's composure under pressure that stood out as he guided India to victory off the final ball of the match. What a remarkable finish! India are the U19 Asia Cup champions! Over 50 339-9 0 Wd 1 1 1 1 4 ( 9 runs) Mohit Ulva 49 (26) Chigurupati Venkata 11 (8) Ahmed Hussain 5-0-38-0 Over Summary View all overs 49.6 4 Ahmed Hussain to Mohit Ulva, FOUR , Mohit Ulva! Remember the name! This is spectacular stuff. India have pulled off a remarkable turnaround, snatching victory from the brink of defeat. And they need to thank this man - Mohit Ulva! Playing a match-defining knock in a tournament final, that too an India-Pakistan final. Stuff of dreams! Mohit Ulva advances down the wicket and smashes the flatter delivery on the shorter side towards the wide long-off boundary. One bounce and into the fence. What a rollicking shot to take India over the line. The Indian players storm on to the field, and it’s a race to get to Mohit Ulva, who has his arms aloft. One Indian player loses his balance and tumbles in the process. Aryan Savsani and Kushagra Ojha lift the hero of the moment on their shoulders. Pure joy and celebration in the Indian camp, with the players blowing flying kisses towards their supporters in the stands Equation: 3 runs needed off the last ball. A tie will take this final to a Super Over 49.5 Ahmed Hussain to Chigurupati Venkata, 1 run, that's a tossed up delivery and Chigurupati Venkata miscues the loft to long-on for a single 49.4 Ahmed Hussain to Mohit Ulva, 1 run, advances down the wicket and drills the tossed up delivery towards long-off for a single 49.3 Ahmed Hussain to Chigurupati Venkata, 1 run, India 333/9, and 5 runs needed now. This was a googly outside off, and Chigurupati Venkata looked to cut and inside-edged onto his pad. The keeper is quick to gather the ball and shy a throw at the bowler's end, but he misses.
